title: Lag is a symptom
briefing: Checkout events are 12 minutes behind. You are the on-call engineer. Investigate using synthetic telemetry, cite evidence, and propose bounded actions. Advance the clock to receive updates.
learning_objective: Separate a slow downstream dependency from consumer capacity, and verify recovery with more than a lag number.

evidence.text: Consumer group checkout: lag 180,000 records, oldest event 12 minutes; producer rate stable at 250/s.
Six consumer workers average 22% CPU. No rebalance events in the last 30 minutes.
Database write p99 increased from 40 ms to 2.8 s after deployment checkout-api-184. Consumers wait on writes.
Service owner confirms checkout-api-183 is compatible with current schema; rollback takes 2 minutes.
Database connection use is 94%. Adding workers would add more database connections.

actions.label: Add two consumer workers
actions.outcome: Two simulated workers requested; connection pressure is intentionally modeled as a tradeoff.

effects.text: After scaling: connection use reaches 100%, write retries rise, and throughput remains 250/s. CPU was not the limiting resource.

actions.label: Roll back the database-writing API deployment
actions.outcome: A simulated rollback request was accepted; verify the resulting telemetry before declaring recovery.

effects.text: Deployment 183 restored. Write p99 is 45 ms, consumer throughput 500/s, and lag is draining.
Oldest event age is below 1 minute. Checkout success and downstream reconciliation match the baseline.

actions.label: Declare recovery and end mitigation
actions.outcome: Recovery declaration recorded using customer and pipeline verification.
